newsitem.title: USA: Cobra Electronics cites strong CB sales.
newsitem.headline: Cobra Electronics cites strong CB sales.

text.p: Cobra Electronics Inc said Thursday its higher 1997 second quarter sales and profits were due to very strong demand for the company's new CB radios and a surge in radar detector shipments both internationally and domestically.

Cobra president and chief executive officer Jerry Kalov said the company has good momentum as it enters the traditionally stronger second half of the year, and he projects continued sales growth and higher earnings for 1997.

Earlier today, Cobra reported 1997 second quarter earnings rose to $1.2 million or $0.20 a share from $284,000 or $0.05 in the second quarter of 1996. Sales increased 37.8 percent from the same quarter last year to $29.5 million.
Gross margin in the second quarter of 1997 remained at 19.3 percent, equal with last year's second quarter.
Internationally, the company benefited from significant growth in the Russian radar detector market.
"We also expect that radar detector shipments in the second half of 1997 will continue to outpace last year's numbers, both domestically and internationally," he said in a news release.
Kalov also said the second half of the year will benefit from increased shipments of the company's new Family Radio Service handheld two-way radios, which began shipments in the current quarter.
Cobra designs and markets consumer electronics products including CB radios, two-way radios, cordless telephones and telephone answering systems.
Shares of Cobra were trading up 3/16 to 6-1/16.
